1.explanation: 1. audits/byte-efficiency/offscreen-images-test.js: This is the unit-test suite for the Offscreen Images audit. It contains the logic that decides which images get flagged, as well as the expectations for how SVGs and zero-area images are handled. Reviewing and updating this file is necessary to verify or change the ignore-SVG behavior. 2. gather/computed/screenshots-test.js: The Offscreen Images audit relies on the “screenshots” computed artifact to collect all elements, their URLs, and their layout bounding rectangles (width & height). Examining this test will show exactly how image elements are discovered, and how their size info is surfaced to the audit. Any change to ignore SVGs would also need to account for how these artifacts are generated.
1.bug_scenario: When running the “Offscreen images” audit against https://www.chromestatus.com/features, Lighthouse picks up an SVG sprite (ring.svg) that has a computed area of zero (width or height == 0) and flags it as an offscreen image with the debug string “Invalid image sizing information …img/ring.svg”. In practice, SVGs often don’t have intrinsic layout sizes in the same way raster images do, so we should be skipping or ignoring .svg assets in this audit.
